engineChanges.change: All Cedar Park values are unverified assumptions; require user to confirm zoning district, plat building lines and adopted code edition before finalizing
SF-2 Single-Family Residential (assumed): use front 25 / side 5 / street side 15 / rear 10 ft as provisional defaults (unverified)
Use IECC Climate Zone 2A prescriptive envelope for the adopted IECC edition
Flag PE-sealed engineered slab (expansive clay east of I-35 / variable limestone and clay in the west)

Check the TCEQ Edwards Aquifer map: lots on the recharge zone (and some in the contributing/transition zones) fall under 30 TAC Chapter 213; regulated development needs an approved Water Pollution Abatement Plan, usually done at subdivision level. Much of Cedar Park is on the recharge zone - assume geologic assessment and water-quality requirements apply unless the subdivision WPAP covers the lot.
Require tree survey; avoid protected/heritage tree root zones or add mitigation cost
Add Cedar Park water + wastewater impact fees (amounts not retrieved)
Most new homes are in PUDs/MUDs or HOA subdivisions - plat building lines, PUD standards and deed restrictions may override district setbacks and add masonry rules

plainLanguage: This Cedar Park file is unverified - our research tools were unavailable, so treat every number as a placeholder. Much of Cedar Park is over the Edwards Aquifer, so state water-quality rules can apply and limit paved area. Large trees are protected and need a survey. Expect water and sewer impact fees. The city cannot require brick, but HOAs often do.
